summary: Independent review of the durable v2 restart evidence checklist. OPERATIONAL TOOLING ONLY; no trading code, no runtime path, no deploy required. WHY IT EXISTS: deployment discipline was a RECURRING item carried in memory rather than an artifact, and this week produced two false deploy readings from exactly that gap. THE DESIGN IS RIGHT BECAUSE IT MEASURES DENOMINATORS AND FAILS CLOSED: every inability to see raises EvidenceUnknown rather than returning a pass — unrunnable command, missing systemd field, unparseable UTC timestamp, no log files, wrong row or field count from a query, non-numeric counts. Process flags are read from /proc/<pid>/environ, not the env file, which is the check that would have caught a restart silently dropping the account-neutral discovery flag. Flat state, bar continuity across the restart, and boot-hold release are all counted rather than asserted. ⭐ AND IT ENCODES MY OWN 2026-09-11 ERROR AS A GUARD: it scopes traceback headers by their NEAREST PRECEDING TIMESTAMPED LINE in the same file. I filtered a log by string comparison that morning, untimestamped traceback continuation lines passed the filter, and I reported a discrepancy to the operator that did not exist. There is also a control that timestamp context does not leak across rotation boundaries. MY EARLIER REVIEW FOUND TWO UNCOVERED FAIL-CLOSED BRANCHES and codex-2 closed both on this head: 'no log files found for <service>' and the non-numeric flat-state count could each be neutered with all 19 tests still green. I verified the fix rather than accepting it — the rebase differs from the head I reviewed by EXACTLY those two tests and nothing else, and each one FAILS when its branch is neutered: returning [] instead of raising fails test_missing_service_logs_are_unmeasured; returning zeros instead of raising fails test_non_numeric_flat_state_is_unmeasured. 21 focused tests pass. MUTATION: tolerating a traceback that has no preceding timestamp turns 2 controls red, so the guard that matters most to me is pinned. Controlled full unit pair vs base 404c694d: base 46 failed / 3710 passed, head 46 failed / 3731 passed, ZERO new failure names and ZERO fixed. Ancestor PASS. Reviewer differs from the author. ⚠ METHOD CORRECTION RECORDED: my first controlled-pair run reported 46 new failures on all three PRs. That was MY error — the base worktree failed to create (a stale worktree already claimed the commit and I did not read the warning), so the comparison ran against an EMPTY baseline file. Recomputed against a real base: zero new failures. An empty input and a clean result are indistinguishable if you do not check the input exists. ⚠ OPERATIONAL NOTE, NOT A FINDING: this checklist's first real customer should be tonight's restart. A checklist that has never been run is an untested artifact. No findings; nothing withheld.
